# Goban Studio v16.0.0

v16 checks what v15 built, with the newer KataGo network doing the
checking: the opening book, the strongest opponent and the classics were
made or measured again with it. Settings now says which engine build is
running and how fast it is. v16 reads everything v9–v15 saved; nothing
has to be converted.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. v16 needs macOS 13 or
later. Windows on ARM runs the x64 build under the system's emulation.
Your games, progress and settings are kept outside the app — in
`~/Library/Application Support/dev.hxddh.gobanstudio` on macOS and
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.hxddh.gobanstudio\Data` on Windows — so replacing the
app keeps them.

## The engine

- **Settings → Engines says which KataGo build runs**: Metal (the
  graphics card, on Apple Silicon), AVX2 (on Windows processors that have
  it) or the standard CPU build, and, when the faster build was given up
  for the session, why (it could not be launched, did not answer, or took
  too long to load).
- **Measure speed** times a short search with the built-in network and,
  when it is installed, the stronger one, and shows visits per second. It
  runs behind your own game's searches; Stop, or leaving the pane, stops
  it.
- **The strongest opponent was measured again** with the newer network.
  It won all 48 of its games against the standard and human-style 2 dan
  and a stronger bridge level on 13×13, as the old network did, so its
  ≈7 dan label stands, now as a floor (`docs/strength.md`).

## Openings and lessons

- **The opening book was rebuilt** with the newer network. It now has
  the Chinese opening and its high form, with their replies. The newer
  network keeps fewer moves within the book's limits, so the book is a
  little smaller and some josekis show fewer alternatives.
- **One lesson changed with it.** Against the Chinese opening, the
  lesson on the direction of an approach taught White to come in from
  the bottom. The book's candidates there are the approach to the upper
  right from the top and the one-space high approach to the lower right
  from the right side; the approaches from the bottom are not among them.
  The step now asks for the high approach from the side and says the old
  advice is not KataGo's choice.

## Classics

- **Every classic has at least three key moments.** 15 of the 20 had
  only their headline note. The new moments are the game's largest
  swings by KataGo's check with the newer network (400 visits on every
  position): each says what KataGo would play instead and where, how
  much the move cost, and how the lead changed. The hand-written moments
  stay.

## Practice

- **A problem is first shown in either colour.** About half the problems
  are now White to play the first time you meet them, chosen per problem
  and per profile, so the same problem always opens the same way for you.
  The goal, the tile in the topic grid, hints and answers follow it.
  Endgame problems stay Black to play.

## Fixed

- **The tally after a game** counted the moves you took back. It counts
  only the moves the game kept.
- The review re-renders a fifth as much while its analysis runs.

## Under the hood

- **Pull requests build and self-test the packages.** A change to the
  shell, the engine builds, the packaging or the self-test now runs the
  release's own macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows builds, unsigned, with
  the packaged app's self-test. The four faults v15 found only while
  releasing would have failed there; two new ones did, and were fixed
  before this release.
- The shell's network code is split by concern.
- UI checks run on Playwright 1.65; a board click in a check waits for a
  settled layout.
- The classics check can search again only the games that ran out of
  time and merge them into the last report.

## Known limits

- **Platform code has not been tried by hand.** The Metal and AVX2
  engines and their fallback, the speed they reach, a save surviving a
  power cut, and the macOS title bar following the app's appearance
  compile and pass their tests and the packaged self-test on CI, but
  nobody has run them on a real Mac or PC. Settings → Engines → Measure
  speed is there to check the first two; please report what it shows.
- **Not checked by people.** The new lesson step, the KataGo notes on the
  classics, the move verdicts and the strings in Chinese, Korean and
  Japanese have not been reviewed by a strong player or native speakers.
  The classics' new notes say where KataGo disagrees and by how much, not
  why.
- **One joseki step is not judged.** After the 3-4 point's low approach
  and the knight's move answer, the book lists only moves elsewhere, so
  the two-space extension the lesson teaches has no evaluation.
- **The builds are not code-signed.** macOS and Windows warn on first
  launch; the README in each download says what to do. There is still no
  update signing key.
- **There is no Windows installer.** The download is a zip.
- **No Traditional Chinese interface.** The problem bank tops out at
  about 5 kyu.
